description: Speed, distance and time, with km/h, m/s and trains

lessons.title: Fast and Slow
lessons.intro: Speed tells us how fast something moves. A faster thing covers more distance in the same time.
explanation: A car and a cycle both travel for 1 hour.
The car covers 60 km. The cycle covers 15 km.
The car covers more distance in the same time, so the car has the greater speed.
lessons.rule: Speed is the distance covered in one unit of time.
lessons.tip: Same time, more distance: that one is faster.

lessons.title: The Speed Formula
lessons.intro: To find speed, divide the distance by the time taken.
explanation: Speed = Distance ÷ Time.
A bus covers 120 km in 3 hours. 120 ÷ 3 = 40.
So the bus travels 40 km in each hour. Its speed is 40 km per hour.
lessons.rule: Speed = Distance ÷ Time.
lessons.tip: Speed is the distance shared equally over the time.

steps.text: A bus covers 120 km in 3 hours. Use the formula.
Divide the distance by the time.
Say the answer with its unit.

lessons.title: Units of Speed
lessons.intro: Speed always has two units in it: one for distance and one for time.
explanation: km/h means kilometres per hour. It is also written km/hr.
m/s means metres per second. It is also written m/sec.
Cars and trains usually use km/h. Runners and short distances usually use m/s.
lessons.rule: The unit of speed is a distance unit per time unit.
lessons.tip: 'Per' means 'in each'. 50 km/h is 50 km in each hour.

lessons.title: Who Is Faster?
lessons.intro: To compare two movers, find each speed in the same unit.
explanation: Asha cycles 36 km in 2 hours. 36 ÷ 2 = 18, so her speed is 18 km/h.
Bilal cycles 51 km in 3 hours. 51 ÷ 3 = 17, so his speed is 17 km/h.
Asha is faster, even though Bilal went further.
lessons.rule: Compare speeds, not distances, to see who is faster.
lessons.tip: Further does not always mean faster. Look at the time too.

lessons.title: Speed per Day or per Minute
lessons.intro: Speed can use any unit of time: a day, a minute or a second.
explanation: A bird flies 125 km each day. That is a speed of 125 km per day.
At that speed a journey of 1,000 km takes 1,000 ÷ 125 = 8 days.
An ant that crawls 15 cm each minute has a speed of 15 cm per minute.
lessons.rule: Whatever the units, speed is still distance divided by time.
lessons.tip: Read the units in the question. They tell you what the answer should look like.

quiz.question: A car covers 150 km in 3 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Divide the distance by the time.

quiz.question: A boy runs 100 metres in 20 seconds. What is his speed in m/s?
quiz.hint: Metres divided by seconds gives m/s.

quiz.question: A train covers 480 km in 6 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Share 480 km equally over 6 hours.

quiz.question: A cyclist rides 45 km in 3 hours. A runner covers 26 km in 2 hours. What is the speed of the faster one, in km/h?
quiz.hint: Find both speeds first, then compare them.

quiz.question: It covers 702 km in 9 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Divide 702 by 9.
quiz.story: The Shatabdi Express is running between Delhi and Bhopal.

quiz.question: It flies 16,500 km at a steady 125 km each day. How many days does the journey take?
quiz.hint: How many lots of 125 km fit into 16,500 km?
quiz.story: A seagull is flying a very long way, from Finland to Australia.

quiz.question: A snail crawls 84 cm in 7 minutes. What is its speed in cm per minute?
quiz.hint: Centimetres divided by minutes.

quiz.question: A plane flies 2,550 km in 3 hours. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Divide 2,550 by 3.

lessons.title: Finding Distance
lessons.intro: If you know the speed and the time, multiply to get the distance.
explanation: Distance = Speed × Time.
A car travels at 60 km/h for 4 hours. 60 × 4 = 240.
It covers 240 km.
lessons.rule: Distance = Speed × Time.
lessons.tip: Speed is the distance for one hour. Multiply by the number of hours.

steps.text: The car covers 60 km in each hour.
It drives for 4 hours. That is four lots of 60.
Say the answer with its unit.

lessons.title: Finding Time
lessons.intro: If you know the distance and the speed, divide to get the time.
explanation: Time = Distance ÷ Speed.
A train must cover 300 km at 75 km/h. 300 ÷ 75 = 4.
The journey takes 4 hours.
lessons.rule: Time = Distance ÷ Speed.
lessons.tip: Ask: how many lots of 75 km fit into 300 km?

lessons.title: One Fact, Three Formulas
lessons.intro: The three formulas are one fact seen three ways. Learn one and you can find the others.
explanation: Speed = Distance ÷ Time.
Distance = Speed × Time.
Time = Distance ÷ Speed.
lessons.rule: Distance is the product. Speed and time are the two numbers that multiply to make it.
lessons.tip: Test with easy numbers. 60 × 2 = 120, so 120 ÷ 2 = 60 and 120 ÷ 60 = 2.

lessons.title: Parts of an Hour
lessons.intro: Times are often given in minutes. Change them to a part of an hour when the speed is in km/h.
explanation: 30 minutes is half an hour, and 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour.
A cyclist rides at 12 km/h. 12 ÷ 2 = 6, so she covers 6 km in half an hour.
12 ÷ 4 = 3, so she covers 3 km in a quarter of an hour.
lessons.rule: For half an hour, halve the hourly distance. For a quarter of an hour, divide it by 4.
lessons.tip: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 20 minutes is one third of an hour.

lessons.title: Answers in Minutes
lessons.intro: Sometimes the time comes out as a part of an hour. Change it to minutes.
explanation: A car travels 18 km at 72 km/h. How long does it take?
72 km/h means 72 km in 60 minutes. 72 ÷ 18 = 4, so 18 km is a quarter of 72 km.
A quarter of the distance takes a quarter of the time. 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so it takes 15 minutes.
lessons.rule: A part of the hourly distance takes the same part of 60 minutes.
lessons.tip: You can also divide 18 by 72 and then multiply by 60. It gives the same answer.

steps.text: 72 km/h means 72 km in 60 minutes.
How many times does 18 km fit into 72 km?
So the car needs a quarter of 60 minutes.

quiz.question: A bus travels at 45 km/h for 4 hours. How many km does it cover?
quiz.hint: Distance is speed times time.

quiz.question: A car must cover 280 km at 70 km/h. How many hours does it take?
quiz.hint: Time is distance divided by speed.

quiz.question: A scooter travels at 40 km/h for 30 minutes. How many km does it cover?
quiz.hint: 30 minutes is half an hour.

quiz.question: A boy walks at 6 km/h. How many minutes does he take to walk 2 km?
quiz.hint: 2 km is one third of 6 km. Take the same part of 60 minutes.

quiz.question: They drive at 50 km/h and the trip takes 3 hours. How many km is the trip?
quiz.hint: Three lots of the distance covered in one hour.
quiz.story: Nikhil's family is driving from Bengaluru to Mysuru.

quiz.question: It crawls 15 cm every minute. How many cm does it crawl in 24 minutes and 40 seconds?
quiz.hint: Find the distance for 24 minutes. Then 40 seconds is two thirds of a minute.
quiz.story: An ant is marching along a wall.

quiz.question: At 90 km/h, how many minutes does a car take to cover 30 km?
quiz.hint: 30 km is one third of 90 km. Take one third of 60 minutes.

quiz.question: A man walks 900 metres in 18 minutes. At the same speed, how many km does he walk in 1 hour?
quiz.hint: Find the metres for 1 minute, then for 60 minutes. Then change metres to km.

lessons.title: Kilometres, Metres, Hours and Seconds
lessons.intro: To change the unit of a speed you need two facts, one for distance and one for time.
explanation: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds.
So 1 hour = 60 × 60 = 3,600 seconds.
lessons.rule: 1 km = 1,000 m and 1 hour = 3,600 seconds.
lessons.tip: Learn these two numbers: 1,000 and 3,600. Every speed conversion uses them.

lessons.title: From km/h to m/s
lessons.intro: To change km/h into m/s, multiply by 5 and divide by 18.
explanation: 18 km/h means 18,000 m in 3,600 seconds.
That is where the 5 and the 18 come from. For 72 km/h, 72 × 5 ÷ 18 = 20, so it is 20 m/s.
lessons.rule: km/h to m/s: multiply by 5, then divide by 18.
lessons.tip: The number gets smaller. A second is short, so only a few metres are covered.

steps.text: Start with the speed in km/h.
Multiply by 5.
Divide by 18.

lessons.title: From m/s to km/h
lessons.intro: To go the other way, multiply by 18 and divide by 5.
explanation: 5 m/s is the same as 18 km/h.
For 30 m/s, 30 × 18 ÷ 5 = 108, so it is 108 km/h.
A quick way: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, and 6 × 18 = 108.
lessons.rule: m/s to km/h: multiply by 18, then divide by 5.
lessons.tip: The number gets bigger. An hour is long, so many kilometres are covered.

lessons.title: Pairs Worth Remembering
lessons.intro: A few conversions come up again and again. Knowing them saves time.
explanation: 18 km/h = 5 m/s.
36 km/h = 10 m/s and 72 km/h = 20 m/s.
54 km/h = 15 m/s, 90 km/h = 25 m/s and 108 km/h = 30 m/s.
lessons.rule: Every 18 km/h is worth 5 m/s.
lessons.tip: Is the km/h number a multiple of 18? Then the conversion is easy.

lessons.title: Match the Units First
lessons.intro: Before you calculate, make sure the units agree.
explanation: A man walks at 6 km/h. How far does he go in 3 minutes?
6 km/h is 6,000 m in 60 minutes. 6,000 ÷ 60 = 100, so he walks 100 m each minute.
100 × 3 = 300, so in 3 minutes he walks 300 m.
lessons.rule: Change the units so that they match before you multiply or divide.
lessons.tip: If the time is in minutes, a speed in metres per minute is easiest.

steps.text: Change 6 km into metres.
He covers 6,000 m in 60 minutes. Find the distance for 1 minute.
Multiply by 3 minutes.

quiz.question: How many metres are there in 7 km?
quiz.hint: Each km is 1,000 m.

quiz.question: Change 36 km/h into m/s.
quiz.hint: Multiply by 5, then divide by 18.

quiz.question: Change 90 km/h into m/s.
quiz.hint: 90 is five lots of 18.

quiz.question: Change 15 m/s into km/h.
quiz.hint: Multiply by 18, then divide by 5.

quiz.question: Its speed is 30 m/s. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Divide by 5 first, then multiply by 18.
quiz.story: A motorcycle is moving along a highway near Pune.

quiz.question: It flies at 10 m/s. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Multiply by 18, then divide by 5.
quiz.story: A dragonfly is darting across a pond.

quiz.question: A girl cycles at 12 km/h. How many metres does she cover in 4 minutes?
quiz.hint: Change 12 km to metres. Find the distance for 1 minute, then for 4.

quiz.question: A car travels 500 metres in 25 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Find the speed in m/s first. Then change it to km/h.

levels.label: Trains and Poles
levels.subtitle: A train covers its own length

lessons.title: A Train Passing a Pole
lessons.intro: When a train passes a pole, it moves forward by exactly its own length.
explanation: The front of the train reaches the pole first.
The train has passed only when its last coach has gone by.
So the distance covered is the length of the train.
lessons.rule: Passing a pole or a standing person: the distance is the length of the train.
lessons.tip: Picture the last coach. It has to travel the whole length of the train.

lessons.title: How Long Does It Take?
lessons.intro: Time is distance divided by speed. Here the distance is the length of the train.
explanation: A train 150 m long runs at 15 m/s.
It takes 10 seconds to pass a pole.
lessons.rule: Time to pass a pole = length of the train ÷ speed.
lessons.tip: Length in metres and speed in m/s give the time in seconds.

steps.text: The distance is the length of the train.
Divide by the speed in m/s.
Say the answer with its unit.

lessons.title: Change km/h to m/s First
lessons.intro: Train lengths are in metres, but speeds are often in km/h. Change the speed first.
explanation: A train 120 m long runs at 36 km/h. How long does it take to pass a pole?
120 ÷ 10 = 12, so it takes 12 seconds.
lessons.rule: Metres go with m/s. Change km/h into m/s before you divide.
lessons.tip: 36 km/h is 10 m/s. That one is worth knowing by heart.

steps.text: Change the speed into m/s.
Divide the length by the speed.

lessons.title: Finding the Speed of a Train
lessons.intro: If you know the length and the time, you can find the speed.
explanation: A train 200 m long passes a pole in 10 seconds.
200 ÷ 10 = 20, so its speed is 20 m/s.
In km/h that is 20 × 18 ÷ 5 = 72 km/h.
lessons.rule: Speed of the train = its length ÷ the time to pass the pole.
lessons.tip: The answer comes in m/s. Change it to km/h if the question asks for that.

lessons.title: Finding the Length of a Train
lessons.intro: If you know the speed and the time, you can find the length.
explanation: A train passes a pole in 28 seconds at 108 km/h. How long is the train?
Length is speed times time. 30 × 28 = 840, so the train is 840 m long.
lessons.rule: Length of the train = speed × time to pass the pole.
lessons.tip: Use m/s and seconds together to get metres.

steps.text: Change the speed into m/s.
Multiply by the time in seconds.

quiz.question: A train 180 m long runs at 20 m/s. How many seconds does it take to pass a pole?
quiz.hint: Divide the length by the speed.

quiz.question: A train 240 m long passes a pole in 12 seconds. What is its speed in m/s?
quiz.hint: Divide the length by the time.

quiz.question: A train runs at 25 m/s and passes a pole in 8 seconds. How many metres long is the train?
quiz.hint: Length is speed times time.

quiz.question: A train 100 m long runs at 36 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass a man standing beside the track?
quiz.hint: Change 36 km/h into m/s first.

quiz.question: The train is 300 m long and its speed is 72 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass the pole?
quiz.hint: Change 72 km/h into m/s, then divide the length by it.
quiz.story: The Rajdhani Express is rushing past a signal pole.

quiz.question: A train 250 m long passes her in 10 seconds without stopping. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: Find the speed in m/s first. Then multiply by 18 and divide by 5.
quiz.story: Zoya is standing on the platform at Nagpur station.

quiz.question: A train running at 54 km/h passes a pole in 20 seconds. How many metres long is the train?
quiz.hint: Change 54 km/h into m/s, then multiply by the time.

quiz.question: A train 200 m long passes a pole in 9 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
quiz.hint: The speed is 200 ÷ 9 m/s. Multiply 200 by 18 first, then divide by 9 and by 5.

levels.label: Journeys with a Twist
levels.subtitle: Clock times, returns and two speeds

lessons.title: Time from the Clock
lessons.intro: Some questions give the start and finish times. Find the time taken first.
explanation: A train leaves at 6:45 pm and arrives at 9:15 pm.
From 6:45 to 8:45 is 2 hours. From 8:45 to 9:15 is 30 minutes.
The journey takes 2 hours 30 minutes, which is 2.5 hours.
lessons.rule: Find the time taken before you use any speed formula.
lessons.tip: Count on in whole hours, then add the minutes that are left.

steps.text: Count the whole hours first: 6:45 to 8:45.
Then the minutes that are left: 8:45 to 9:15.
30 minutes is half an hour, which is 0.5 hours.

lessons.title: Clock Times and Distance
lessons.intro: Now use the time taken to find the distance.
explanation: The train above travels for 2.5 hours at 80 km/h.
The two cities are 200 km apart.
lessons.rule: Use the time taken, in hours, with a speed in km/h.
lessons.tip: 2.5 hours is 2 hours and half an hour. 80 × 2 = 160, and half of 80 is 40. 160 + 40 = 200.

lessons.title: The Return Journey
lessons.intro: On a return trip the distance stays the same. Only the speed and the time change.
explanation: Nirav drives 360 km in 6 hours. On the way back he drives 15 km/h slower.
Going: 360 ÷ 6 = 60, so his speed is 60 km/h. Coming back: 60 − 15 = 45, so his speed is 45 km/h.
360 ÷ 45 = 8, so the return takes 8 hours.
lessons.rule: Same road, new speed: find the new speed, then divide the distance by it.
lessons.tip: The distance does not change on the way back.

steps.text: Find the speed on the way there.
Find the slower speed on the way back.
The distance is the same. Divide it by the new speed.

lessons.title: Two Parts, Two Speeds
lessons.intro: When a journey has parts at different speeds, find the time for each part.
explanation: Shreya runs 100 m at 4 m/s and then 300 m at 5 m/s.
First part: 100 ÷ 4 = 25 seconds. Second part: 300 ÷ 5 = 60 seconds.
Total time: 25 + 60 = 85 seconds.
lessons.rule: Find the time for each part separately, then add the times.
lessons.tip: Never add the two speeds. Add the times.

lessons.title: Walking and Riding
lessons.intro: Some puzzles mix two ways of travelling. Break each trip into one-way parts.
explanation: Amar walks to school and rides back. That takes 40 minutes altogether. Walking both ways takes 60 minutes.
Walking one way takes 60 ÷ 2 = 30 minutes. So riding one way takes 40 − 30 = 10 minutes.
Riding both ways takes 10 × 2 = 20 minutes.
lessons.rule: Split each trip into one-way parts, then build the trip you need.
lessons.tip: Both ways is double one way. One way is half of both ways.

steps.text: Walking both ways takes 60 minutes. Halve it for one way.
One walk and one ride take 40 minutes. Take away the walk.
Double it for riding both ways.

quiz.question: A bus leaves at 2:15 pm and arrives at 5:45 pm. How many minutes does the journey take?
quiz.hint: Count the whole hours first, then the extra minutes. Each hour is 60 minutes.

quiz.question: A car travels for 2.5 hours at 60 km/h. How many km does it cover?
quiz.hint: Find the distance for 2 hours, then add the distance for half an hour.

quiz.question: Meena runs 200 m at 5 m/s and then 300 m at 6 m/s. How many seconds does she take altogether?
quiz.hint: Find the time for each part, then add the two times.

quiz.question: A man drives 240 km in 4 hours. On the way back he drives 20 km/h slower. How many hours does the return journey take?
quiz.hint: Find his speed on the way there. Take 20 off for the way back.

quiz.question: The train leaves at 6:45 pm and arrives at 9:15 pm the same day. Its speed is 30 m/s. How many km apart are the two cities?
quiz.hint: Find the time taken in hours. Change the speed into km/h. Then multiply.
quiz.story: A fast train runs between Mumbai and Surat in the evening.

quiz.question: He covers 680 km in 8 hours on the way there. On the way back he drives 17 km/h slower. How many minutes does the return journey take?
quiz.hint: Find the first speed, then the slower speed, then the time in hours. Each hour is 60 minutes.
quiz.story: Nirav is driving from Ahmedabad to Indore and back.

quiz.question: Amar walks from A to B and rides back in 37 minutes altogether. Walking both ways takes him 55 minutes. How many minutes does riding both ways take?
quiz.hint: Halve 55 to get one walk. Take that from 37 to get one ride. Then double it.

quiz.question: Shraddha runs 5 rounds of a 400 m track. In each round she runs the first 100 m at 4 m/s and the remaining 300 m at 5 m/s. How many seconds does she take for all 5 rounds?
quiz.hint: Find the time for one round first: the time for 100 m plus the time for 300 m.
